sections.h2: Does Texas tax inheritances or estates?
sections.html:
Texas repealed its inheritance tax. Senate Bill 752 (2015) ended it effective September 1, 2015, removing Tax Code Chapter 211, according to the Comptroller's records.

That leaves the federal estate tax as the main death tax an heir hears about, and it applies only to large estates. What heirs of a Texas house face more often is property tax, probate paperwork and deed recording, covered below.

sections.h2: When does the federal estate tax apply to a Texas estate?
sections.html:
A federal return is required only when the gross estate, plus adjusted taxable gifts and the specific gift tax exemption, is worth more than the filing threshold for the year of death. The IRS says most simple estates do not need to file.

IRS estate tax filing thresholds by year of death
Year of deathFiling threshold
2023$12,920,000
2024$13,610,000
2025$13,990,000
2026$15,000,000

These are filing thresholds, not tax rates. The IRS counts the fair market value of everything owned at death, including real estate, and allows deductions for mortgages and other debts, administration expenses, and property passing to a surviving spouse or qualified charity. A surviving spouse may elect to carry over the decedent's unused exemption on a timely filed return.

sections.h2: How does a Texas house pass to heirs?
sections.html:
The route depends on whether there is a will and how the estate is handled. Texas State Law Library guides describe several paths, and each leaves a different paper trail in the county clerk's records.

  • Probate of a will: the window is four years from death, though a court may accept a later filing for an acceptable reason.
  • Muniment of title: used when the estate owes nothing beyond real-estate liens or needs no administration; the court order and will are filed with the clerk of the county where the property sits.
  • Small estate affidavit under Estates Code Chapter 205: for estates with assets of $75,000 or less, not counting homestead and exempt property, and with court approval.
  • Affidavit of heirship: a sworn statement filed with the county clerk that no law forces a third party to accept.
  • Transfer on death deed: passes real property without probate if recorded before the owner's death.

sections.h2: What does a small estate affidavit require?
sections.html:
It requires no will, no pending administration, assets of $75,000 or less excluding homestead and exempt property, and enough assets to pay debts. All heirs must agree, and the court must approve it.

The affidavit may not cover real property other than a homestead that passes to a spouse or minor children. The county clerk manual adds that two disinterested witnesses swear to it, at least 30 days must have passed since death, and no petition for a personal representative can be pending or granted. A copy covering a homestead is recorded with the county clerk.

sections.h2: What deed does an heir need to sell inherited Texas property?
sections.html:
The deed type follows the estate route, and a buyer's title company will look for the matching recorded document.

  • Transfer on death deed: an affidavit of death and the death certificate recorded in the county where the property sits.
  • Administered estate: an executor's or administrator's deed.
  • Muniment of title: the court order and the will.
  • No court process: an affidavit of heirship.

The county cannot add heirs to the old deed. Whatever the route, the recorded instrument must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer, and the fees follow the clerk's schedule: $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page in the 2023 manual, plus the records fees listed there.

sections.h2: What property tax does an inherited house carry?
sections.html:
Property tax keeps running through probate. Appraisal districts value property as of January 1, and a tax lien attaches on that date to secure the year's taxes, penalties and interest, regardless of who inherits.

  • Bills go out around October 1, and taxes unpaid on February 1 are delinquent.
  • On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added; the penalty rises to 12 percent on July 1.
  • Heirs who are not on a recorded deed need an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation to claim the homestead exemption.
  • A surviving spouse aged 55 or older may keep the deceased spouse's over-65 exemption in certain cases.

A homestead's appraised value is capped at a 10 percent yearly rise once the exemption has been in place, which can help heirs who keep the house for a while.

sections.h2: How does selling an inherited house change the picture?
sections.html:
A sale settles the property tax, mortgage and any recorded liens from the proceeds at closing, and the heirs split what is left according to the estate route. Sellers should line up the recorded deed, the payoff figures and the tax statement before accepting an offer.

Federal rules on income tax for gains and on gifts are separate from the estate tax filing thresholds above, so ask a tax professional about them. For the Texas side, ask the county tax office for a payoff and the county clerk for copies of what is recorded against the title.

faqs.q: Does Texas have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. Texas repealed it effective September 1, 2015 under Senate Bill 752, which removed Tax Code Chapter 211.

faqs.q: What is the federal estate tax filing threshold in 2026?
faqs.a: The IRS lists $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026 and $13,990,000 for deaths in 2025. These are filing thresholds, not rates.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax on a house I inherited?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax attaches to the property through a lien that arises each January 1. Bills go out around October 1, and unpaid taxes are delinquent after January 31.

faqs.q: How long do I have to probate a will in Texas?
faqs.a: Four years from the date of death, though a court may accept a later filing for an acceptable reason, per the Texas State Law Library.

faqs.q: Can I sell inherited property without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A recorded transfer on death deed passes property without probate, and a muniment of title or small estate affidavit may fit smaller or simpler estates. Ask the county clerk what your title company will accept.
